what_it_does: Elastic SSDs (ESSDs) are network-attached solid-state storage drives offered by cloud providers like AWS and Alibaba Cloud; unlike a physical SSD plugged into a server, an ESSD is a remote storage service accessed over a high-speed network, with capacity and performance that can be dialed up or down on demand. Many teams assume they can swap a local SSD for an ESSD and get similar behaviour, but the internal architecture and network path make ESSDs behave differently in ways that are poorly documented. This paper runs a comprehensive set of storage benchmarks on two production ESSDs and catalogues their real-world performance characteristics — including surprising or counterintuitive patterns in latency and throughput under different access sizes, queue depths, and read/write mixes. The goal is to turn implicit, undocumented assumptions (the 'unwritten contract') into explicit, measured knowledge that cloud software developers and storage architects can rely on when deciding how to use or optimize around ESSDs.
